column3: But I always got really shaken up whenever I did get in trouble, with them or anyone else.
It was crushing.
It was ridiculous, but every time it felt like I was about to be char-broiled and executed.
Talk about an overreaction.
So, to avoid that feeling, I got used to living my life the way others thought I should:
Wake up, go to school, do the work, come home, study, go to sleep,
Rinse, lather, repeat.
Just like all other 7 billion whatever people on this planet.
Automatic process; automatic life.
Stay in line, wait for the mid-life crisis to kick in.
All of it is just so pointless.
Then I met her.
I met the real her-- not that doll.
She really... opened my eyes.
If it's pointless anyway, you may as well have fun with it, she said.
Break the rules, color outside of the lines-- why not?
Isn't it better than living a cookie-cutter life?
She went on to do just that.
She found me, and recruited me to the team to help rescue her.
I found freedom under her power.
Because with her, the rules didn't matter anyway.
She was in it for the same reason--
Everything is awful; may as well have some fun.
I think I was the only person she trusted, because we had that in common.
There's probably a lot I could tell you about her and her plans.
But I don't think she'd want that.
Even now, she's probably watching.
Aren't you?
Did you bring me back out of pity?
Or was it boredom?
TERRA: ...It looks like I'm left out to guess at it now too.
I don't care enough to.
I didn't ask to come back.
Better to go out with a bang than burn out and fade away.
And I don't think I have that much zaniness left in me anyway.
What about you?
Did you find it funny-- all of my antics before?
TERRA: Well, that's nice I guess.
TERRA: Just obnoxious, right?
Sometimes I even annoyed myself with it all.
But it's better than withering away under monotony.
That's what I told myself.
I shouldn't still be here.
TERRA: Just let me go.
Both of you.
Yes

Now that you've had your moment.
But whatever.
I guess it's just gonna be like that.
But thanks,
I guess.

Despite everything before, you're pretty solid.
Thanks for the assist, I guess.
I'm gonna be the bigger person and keep on smiling despite all this.
...But anyway, it looks like this operation's a bust.
That Mew is slippery, and...
Well, I guess I messed this one up.
My bad, \PN.
Maybe next time.
I'll see you back at the Nightclub.

FERN: Sure, of course you'd have your own stuff still.
See ya.
FERN: I think I see the switch right behind you...
If you could just... flip that...
That'd be cool.
FERN: ...
All right, I know.
This is payback for what happened in Rhodochrine.
And you know what?
You're entitled to that.
So, go ahead, let it out; have your laugh, your moment, sure.
And then come back and let me out.
Yeah?
What are you even doing this for, huh?
Can't you just let me out?
What'd I ever do to you?
FERN: ...What, do you want me to get on my knees and beg?
Beg like you did?
Even you eventually refused to do that.
Are you really gonna make me do it now?
Is this what you're into?
This really the only way we're gonna do this?
FERN: You're really doing this to me, huh.
This level of pettiness is pretty cringe, but...
Whatever floats your boat, I guess.
Fine, let's do it.
O glorious savior \PN, I, Fern, prostrate myself before you in hopes of your mercy.
Hear my plea and be generous in thy sentencing...
FERN: Sigh...
You're really gonna have me go through the whole thing, huh.
Whatever.
I, Fern, admit that I am an inferior Trainer, battler, and person, to \PN.
...Isn't that enough?
FERN: ...Sigh.
I, Fern, swear that I will never get in \PN's way, because I'm not worth the time it takes to step on me...
Can we be done?
FERN: ...You are really pushing this too far, fam.
...I, Fern, fully embrace the fact that I will NEVER be anywhere remotely near as cool, stylish, popular, talented, good-looking, or likable as \PN.
Bet it's easy to feel secure in that one with my face like this, huh.
Are we done now though?
We're good?
Got that out of your system?
Wanna call me 'princess' too while you're at it?
Or can we all finally go home now?

For some reason someone graffitied those ruins with numbers and bright paint. Baby's first graffiti I'm guessing.

Good luck on that one-- I don't envy you.

I was supposed to find some cute, defenseless Electric Type, and well, this was technically one of those...
But a Geodude?

Lure the Pokémon here, weaken it a bit, and to keep pests away.
How hard is that?
I should've known not to hire scum from Orre.
But those fools were the first team available, and with all the reports of Legendaries popping up in this region, I couldn't afford to wait...
You get what you pay for, I guess.
Nothing more can be expected from these bottom-of- the-bargain-bin foreigners.
But once I have this Pokémon-- a Mythical like this valued for its speed and attack power...
It'll be worth millions! And a powerhouse to boot.
Notice it's not zipping around now like before.
It's because it knows.
In the face of true power-- born leadership and control like mine-- any Pokémon would submit!
It's only natural, after all-- a Pokémon like this suits someone like me.
Mythical-- a class above everyone else!

Maybe I'll take them along with this Zeraora once I'm done.
This is my lucky day!
Enough!

Something like noble poachers,
Stealin' from those who want to cage and abuse Pokémon...
Nothing's set in stone yet, but it's an idea.

I'll keep you safe and sound just the same, sure as the sun shines.

Thanks for tuning into this one with me.
I think we did some good here.

CAL: Well, let's go ahead and get started.
Now that we've settled on a site, we'll each do proper introductions.
Afterwards we can get the tents up and take a rest.
Let's each of us begin by saying who we are, and what we hope to get out of this week.
For my part, I'm someone who's just learning to take the first true steps towards agency and peace.
I've got a lot of self-discovery left to do, which is why I'm grateful, not just for the chance to be here,
But for the chance to lead this trip, and have some of my closest friends alongside me during it.
I hope that by the end of this week, I have a clearer picture of myself disconnected from the recent chaotic events,
And that I will have earned the genuine trust and vulnerability of each of you, both as an individual and a leader in the Academy.
LETTIE: I still can't believe Victoria picked YOU.
CAL: I can hardly believe it myself, so I understand your concerns.
But despite-- or, perhaps because of-- my past, I have the sincere belief that I can give my all to Apophyll Academy and live up to the opportunity.
Now, who would like to go next?
PRESTON: Sure, I'll go.
My name's Preston, and I'm hoping to just have a nice week out in nature and unwind for a bit.
CAL: And who are you?
PRESTON: I... just said, my name's Preston.
CAL: I'm not asking for your name.
Who are you?
PRESTON: Uhh...
Well, I work as a system manager for a preservation initiative on Azurine Island--
CAL: Is your profession who you are?
PRESTON: I--
Man, what do you want from me here?
CAL: I apologize if I'm coming on strong here, but you've fallen for the trap.
System manager may be your job title.
But-- and you can answer 'yes' to this, if you'd like-- is it who you are?
Who you want to represent yourself as?
Or is it just a summative label of how you spend your time under the notion that one's profession is the thing most people want to know about you?
PRESTON: I, uh...
Well, shit.
CAL: Take your time. It is not an easy question.
But if we can't be faithful to ourselves in how we represent ourselves, how can we hope for anyone else to see us faithfully?
The work begins now.
